title: Dominic and the Autopsy
premise: Emrys Dunmore, a true-crime podcaster who has spent years dissecting other people's tragedies from a safe distance, receives two letters about the forty-year-old Dunmore family autopsy case: one confessing to the death of his great-uncle, one promising that 'the second body is still warm.' As Emrys investigates, he discovers the confession is false—written by his own estranged mother to protect someone—and that the real killer lives within the family he never belonged to. The climax comes at the exhumation hearing where Emrys exposes the true killer, his grandfather's old business partner turned family patriarch, and in doing so must choose between exposing his mother's obstruction and finally claiming his place in a family built on a lie. He closes the case, keeps her secret, and finds belonging not in blood but in truth-telling.
about_author: Y. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former coroner's assistant who spent a decade writing case summaries before turning to fiction. They live on the Welsh coast with two indifferent cats and an archive of unsolved cases.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes
chapters.summary: Emrys records the finale of his podcast season, feeling hollow despite success, when twin letters arrive—one confessing to the 1984 Dunmore autopsy death, one promising more. His POV establishes his detachment and hunger for connection. Emotional beat: unease disguised as excitement; the confession bears handwriting he almost recognizes.

chapters.title: The Case Everyone Closed
chapters.summary: Emrys digs into the original file: his great-uncle Aneurin died on an autopsy table, ruled accidental, sealed by court order. His POV alternates with podcast narration excerpts. Emotional beat: obsession kindling as he realizes the case touches his own bloodline—a family that erased him.

chapters.title: Mother Tongue
chapters.summary: Emrys confronts his estranged mother, Nesta, who denies everything but flinches at the letters. Her POV reveals she recognized the handwriting instantly. Emotional beat: guarded love curdling into fear; she burns something in the garden sink after he leaves.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys visits Dunmore Hall under pretense of a podcast interview, meeting patriarch Idris Vaughan and his brittle heirs. His POV catalogs their rehearsed grief. Emotional beat: seduction and wrongness—he wants to belong here even as every portrait seems to watch him leave.

chapters.title: Second Body
chapters.summary: A second letter arrives with a photograph of an unmarked grave behind the Hall. Nesta's POV shows her drafting a counter-confession, revealing fragments: she saw something as a child in 1984. Emotional beat: dread tightening; the promise in letter two was literal.

chapters.title: What the Table Said
chapters.summary: Emrys tracks down the retired mortuary attendant who assisted in 1984, who admits the body was moved before the official autopsy—someone swapped or tampered. His POV. Emotional beat: vertigo; the closed case was closed deliberately, and his mother's name appears in the visitor log.

chapters.title: Confession, Counterfeit
chapters.summary: Handwriting analysis confirms letter one was written by Nesta—but recently, and copied from an older document. Her POV breaks open: she wrote it to force the case reopened on her terms before Idris could bury it again. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with understanding; she was protecting Emrys all along.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Emrys discovers Aneurin's will named him—unborn then—as contingent heir, voided only if the death remained 'natural.' Idris summons him with veiled threats. His POV. Emotional beat: cold clarity; his invisibility was engineered, and the killer has been managing him since letter one.

chapters.title: Exhumation
chapters.summary: At the hearing Emrys springs his trap: the swapped body, the forged closure, Idris's fingerprints on both letters' chain of custody. Idris unravels publicly, confessing to silence and murder. His POV amid chaos. Emotional beat: triumphant terror—the trial begins, and Nesta is subpoenaed next.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Nesta testifies to what she witnessed as a child; Emrys shields her from perjury by reframing her letters as evidence, not crime. Mother and son reconcile over Aneurin's true grave. His closing POV. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—identity claimed not through inheritance but through the courage to look.
